recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for core FHIR. If the same behavior still matters, verify it in the current Java tooling/library repository or raise a reproducible current tooling issue rather than changing core specification source.
issue_request: FHIR-5567 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core correction for the Java Reference Implementation used against DEV/DSTU2 servers, requesting fixes to ResourceAddress, ResourceRequest, ResourceFormat, ClientUtils, FHIRSimpleClient, and cautious XmlParserBase handling.
initial_application: No commit explicitly names FHIR-5567, but the Jira says the fixes were made in SVN around revision 3993. Git-svn commit 67be44c74ca7f899a986ba663a9d11d19c5f9dd3 at SVN r3978 applied the main Java RI client patch, and b3ab25795456ed8b145865a9f7b5c1446930f183 at SVN r3982 handled the XmlParserBase/id parsing concern through the related FHIR-4026 parser fix.
additional_context: The org.hl7.fhir.instance Java RI files were deleted in the 2015 Java RI refactor, and later old/generated Java implementation trees were moved and removed during the 2019 refactor. Current source has no tracked implementations/java, tools/java, or build/implementations/java tree, and source/fhir.ini has no build entry for the affected Java RI files.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because the affected code is historical/outside the current FHIR core source scope and there is no current specification source file to edit.

related_jiras.note: The XmlParserBase concern in FHIR-5567 overlaps the separate Published parser issue fixed in SVN r3982; it was used as background evidence but not separately decided here.
